title: Indexes [CREATE INDEX]
description:
## Indexes
Without an index, SQL scans EVERY row to find what you're looking for. With millions of rows, that's slow.

An index is like a book's index - instead of reading every page, you jump straight to what you need.
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_name ON servers(name);
```
Now `WHERE name = 'prod-1'` is fast because SQL uses the index instead of scanning.

### When to use indexes:
- Columns you search by often (WHERE)
- Columns you JOIN on
- Columns you ORDER BY

### When NOT to:
- Small tables (not worth it)
- Columns that change constantly (index has to rebuild)

To delete an index:
```sql
DROP INDEX idx_name;
```
